title: Progressive Response Diffing and Delta Contract Playbook
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the contract and operational standards for progressively-delivered response diffs ("progressive diffs") between Redwood API servers and clients. Progressive diffs reduce tail latency and bandwidth for large structured outputs (e.g., long-form generation, document syntheses, reranking results) while preserving a deterministic reassembly model and clear failure modes.

Use cases:
- Streaming long-form text where early tokens allow UI responsiveness while the rest is produced.
- Large structured outputs (JSON arrays, embeddings batches) where incremental updates reduce re-render cost and cost-per-token.
- Reranking or multi-pass synthesis where final quality is produced after several refinement passes.

Goals and constraints:
- Make client merge logic simple and robust (checksum-verified patches).
- Guarantee monotonic, replayable sequences to support resume and auditing.
- Bound server-side memory and outstanding delta windows per session.
- Provide clear telemetry to detect reconstruction failures and excess bandwidth.

Contract summary (high level):
- Server emits a sequence of messages for each request: full_response (optional initial snapshot), then delta messages with monotonically increasing seq_id integers, concluding with terminal message (complete=true).
- Each delta contains: seq_id, base_version (server-side logical version), patch_blob (binary or base64), patch_type ("json-patch" | "append" | "replace-range"), checksum (sha256 hex), and hint headers for client backpressure.
- Clients must apply deltas in order; if a gap is detected the client must call the resync endpoint.

Config table (required fields and constraints):
| field | type | description | constraints |
| seq_id | integer | Monotonic sequence identifier | Increasing by 1 from initial seq; start at 1 |
| base_version | string | Server artifact version this delta targets | Semver-like string or build id |
| patch_type | enum | Patch encoding | One of: json-patch, append, replace-range |
| patch_blob | bytes/base64 | Patch payload | Max size 65536 bytes (64KB) unless negotiated |
| checksum | hex string | SHA256 of resulting object after apply or of patch_blob depending on type | Required |
| complete | boolean | Marks terminal message | Exactly one message with complete=true per request |
| session_hint | string | Optional backpressure hint (e.g., "slow-client") | Max length 64 |

Operational SLOs and thresholds:
- Reassembly success rate: 99.95% over 30d for hosted API production traffic.
- Resync latency: median <= 30ms, p95 <= 200ms for resync endpoint.
- Max outstanding deltas per session: default 16; in high-throughput customers negotiable (max 64).
- Max patch_blob size default: 64KB, negotiable per client capability during handshake.
- If client cannot keep up (queue growth), server must emit session_hint: "throttle" and reduce delta frequency by 2x within 1s.

Client merge algorithm (required):
1) Validate incoming message headers: verify seq_id increments by 1.
2) Validate checksum: if checksum fails, mark state=STALE and call /v1/resync?request_id=<id>&from_seq=<last_good_seq+1>.
3) Apply patch according to patch_type atomically.
4) Emit local event: response_partial_updated(seq_id).
5) When complete=true received and post-apply checksum matches server-provided final_checksum, mark request COMPLETE.
6) If resync fails after 3 attempts with exponential backoff (100ms, 300ms, 1s), surface user-visible degraded state and fall back to retrieving a full snapshot (/v1/full-response).

Server responsibilities (required):
- Maintain deterministic patch generation for a request_id: identical base_version implies same patch stream.
- Limit delta window per session to configured outstanding count. Reject new deltas with HTTP 429 + Retry-After when exceeded.
- Provide resync endpoint that returns the minimal required sequence of deltas or a full snapshot if cheaper.
- Emit telemetry tags described below on each delta and final message.
- If any delta encoding would exceed negotiated size, server should emit early partials (split semantics) rather than a single oversized delta.

Failure modes and error codes (API mapping):
- 409 RESOURCE_MISMATCH: client applied a different base_version causing checksum mismatch — trigger resync.
- 429 DELTA_WINDOW_EXCEEDED: too many outstanding deltas; includes Retry-After header.
- 422 PATCH_INVALID: patch malformed (e.g., invalid json-patch ops).
- 500 INTERNAL_DELTA_ERROR: server failed to compute or stream delta — fallback to full snapshot.

Backwards-compatibility and handshake negotiation:
- Clients and servers negotiate progressive diff capability during initial HTTP/1.1 Upgrade or HTTP/2 SETTINGS / WebSocket subprotocol. The handshake includes: max_delta_size, max_outstanding_deltas, preferred_patch_types (ordered).
- Servers must accept unknown fields in handshake and ignore them. If client does not advertise capability, server must default to non-delta full-response behavior.

Telemetry and required metrics/traces (naming conventions):
- metric.delta.count (tags: env, region, model, patch_type, success:boolean)
- metric.delta.resync_rate (tags: env, region)
- metric.delta.reassembly_failures (tags: error_code)
- trace span names: gateway-service/emit-delta, delta-orchestrator/compute-patch, response-assembler/apply-patch.
- Log contract: every terminal message must include fields: request_id, user_id, model, seq_last, total_bytes, reassembly_checksum. These fields are required for post-incident triage.

Testing and rollout checklist (gating criteria):
- Unit tests: patch generators and client merge logic exercised with randomized patches and out-of-order injection.
- Integration tests: simulated packet loss and reordering with resync exercised.
- Performance tests: delta path must not increase median CPU per request by >5% vs baseline for equivalent payloads.
- Canary rollout: 1% traffic for 48 hours; monitor reassembly_failures and resync_rate; if reassembly_failures > 0.05% or resync_rate increases by >5x vs baseline, roll back.

Example payloads and commands:
- Example delta message (JSON over streaming channel):
{
  "request_id": "req_12345",
  "seq_id": 3,
  "base_version": "v20250114-7e2f",
  "patch_type": "json-patch",
  "patch_blob": "[ { "op": "add", "path": "/paragraphs/2", "value": "New paragraph text..." } ]",
  "checksum": "f6a8d1...",
  "complete": false
}

- Resync example (curl):
curl -X GET "https://api.redwood.com/v1/resync?request_id=req_12345&from_seq=2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

Server response (on resync success):
{ "request_id":"req_12345", "deltas":[ /* ordered delta messages */ ] }
